choiceTexts: Neither changes until the leaf runs out of carbon dioxide

answer.line: Darkness stops the steps that need ATP. 3-PGA is made but not used, so it piles up; RuBP is used but not rebuilt.

steps: Split the cycle at RuBisCO. Fixation, RuBP plus CO2 to 3-PGA, needs no ATP; using 3-PGA and rebuilding RuBP both need ATP.
Turn off the light and ATP and NADPH run out within seconds. 3-PGA keeps being made but stops being used, so it piles up.
RuBisCO keeps using RuBP for a few seconds, and none is rebuilt. RuBP falls.

choices.note: That is the pattern when CO2 runs out with the light on: fixation stops, RuBP piles up and 3-PGA drains.
3-PGA does rise. RuBP is still being used and no longer rebuilt, so it cannot rise.
RuBP does fall. But fixation keeps running for a few seconds, so 3-PGA builds up instead of dropping.

choices.text: Neither changes until the leaf runs out of carbon dioxide
choices.note: The Calvin cycle needs ATP and NADPH from the light reactions, so darkness shows up within seconds. The old name, dark reactions, misleads here.
Made but not used piles up; used but not rebuilt drains.

lockIt: Block a step: the molecule just before it piles up, and the one just after it drains.

legend.label: Fixation by RuBisCO: needs no ATP, so it keeps running for a few seconds
Reduction: ATP and NADPH turn 3-PGA into G3P; stopped in the dark
Regeneration: ATP rebuilds RuBP from G3P; stopped in the dark

swatches.label: crossed, dashed arrows: steps that stop without ATP

visual.alt: The Calvin cycle in the dark. RuBisCO still joins RuBP and CO2 into 3-PGA, which needs no ATP, but the two arrows that need ATP, 3-PGA to G3P (which also needs NADPH) and G3P back to RuBP, are crossed out. RuBP, marked falls, and 3-PGA, marked piles up, are outlined as the answer.
visual.caption: Find the crossed-out arrows. The box before them piles up; the box they used to refill drains.
